1	\begin{abstract}
2	Test-time compute scaling yields large gains on discrete-answer reasoning and code generation, yet for named entity recognition (NER), where outputs are entity sets with partial overlap, aggregation gains are marginal relative to their inference cost.
3	We diagnose this \textbf{correlation-selection gap} and provide entity-level workarounds that bypass it.
4	A four-stage diagnostic cascade localizes where aggregation underperforms: quality signals correlate with oracle F1 (Spearman $\rho$ up to 0.45) across nine method categories, yet majority vote yields only $+0.2$--$0.6$\,pp at $N{\geq}32$ while LP-based selection achieves larger gains at $N{=}8$---near-zero selection alignment ($\alpha{\to}0$), not degeneracy alone, is a major contributing factor.
5	Entity-level LP-weighted construction ($+0.3$--$1.4$\,pp) and regime-specific LP selection ($+1.39$\,pp on Few-NERD) bypass the sample-level bottleneck by operating at entity granularity.
6	A degeneracy threshold ($\theta_{\text{crit}}{=}0.70$) predicts when aggregation gains vanish, with preliminary extensions to RE and SQL parsing.
7	\end{abstract}

The question has practical stakes beyond information extraction.
Hallucination detection methods such as SelfCheckGPT \cite{manakul2023selfcheckgpt} and FActScore \cite{min2023factscore} rely on cross-sample consistency to verify individual claims: if a model's outputs agree, the shared content is presumed factual.
This reasoning assumes entity-level self-verification works, that a model can reliably distinguish correct extractions from incorrect ones through self-judgment or re-prompting.
We show this assumption fails.
Three independent probes (entity self-judgment, multi-round re-prompting, latent-space aggregation) all yield chance-level or negative results for a fine-tuned 8B model on NER.
Recent work \cite{yao2026consistency} shows task-level correlation ($\rho$ up to 0.47) between consistency and accuracy but does not diagnose \textit{when} or \textit{why} this correlation fails at the selection level, nor identify entity-level mechanisms to bypass the gap.
Our diagnostic framework addresses this question: four failure modes (degeneracy, low agreement, false agreement, LP compression) characterize how strong instance-level correlation coexists with negligible sample-level selection gain.

We call this disparity the \textbf{correlation-selection gap}.
Five quality estimation (QE) signals achieve rank correlations up to $\rho{=}0.45$ and AUROC up to 0.82 with oracle F1, yet majority vote yields only marginal gains---$+0.2$--$0.6$\,pp on CoNLL at $N{\geq}32$, near zero on SciERC (3-seed mean ${\approx}0$ at $N{=}32$), and persistently negative on Few-NERD through $N{=}16$ (Figure~\ref{fig:n_scaling}; Table~\ref{tab:selection}).

To test whether entity-level methods can close this gap, we evaluated nine method categories spanning prompt-based self-verification, latent-space aggregation, and supervised classifiers (Table~\ref{tab:method_summary}).
No method produces statistically significant F1 improvement over majority vote on any tested configuration across three NER datasets and two model families (Appendix~\ref{app:method_coverage}).
A supervised hidden-state probe achieves entity-level AUROC${=}0.63$\textendash$0.88$ from a single forward pass, exceeding prompt-based self-judgment (${=}0.51$) but not uniformly exceeding multi-sample agreement (${=}0.87$)---an introspection boundary modulated by task complexity (\S\ref{sec:mechanistic}).

These findings rest on controlled experiments across four NER benchmarks (SciERC \cite{luan2018scierc}, Few-NERD \cite{ding2021fewnerd}, CoNLL-2003 \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll}, WNUT-17 \cite{derczynski2017wnut}), two model families (Qwen3-8B, LLaMA-3.1-8B), 4B/14B ablations, and sample sizes $N {\in} \{2, \ldots, 64\}$.

A supervised hidden-state probe confirms that entity quality is partially encoded internally (AUROC${=}0.63$\textendash$0.88$, exceeding self-judgment at $0.51$ but not multi-sample agreement at $0.87$; \S\ref{sec:mechanistic}).
The information to distinguish good from bad outputs exists, yet three self-verification probes (entity self-judgment, multi-round re-prompting, latent-space aggregation) all yield chance-level results for fine-tuned models, exposing an \textit{introspection boundary} \cite{huang2024large}.

This population-level reliability makes the instance-level failure all the more striking.
We call the disparity the \textbf{correlation-selection gap}: majority vote yields only $+0.2$--$0.6$\,pp on CoNLL at $N{\geq}32$, near zero on SciERC (3-seed mean ${\approx}0$ at $N{=}32$), and persistently negative on Few-NERD through $N{=}16$ (Figure~\ref{fig:n_scaling}; Table~\ref{tab:selection}).
The optimal strategy is dataset-dependent (LP-based selection: $+1.39$\,pp on Few-NERD, Holm $p_{\text{adj}}{=}0.021$; MV: $+0.61$ vs.\ LP $-2.34$\,pp on CoNLL at $N{=}64$).
A four-stage diagnostic cascade localizes the failure: degeneracy ($12$--$68$\%) reduces the candidate pool, LP compression flattens score differences, and near-zero selection alignment ($\alpha{\to}0$) prevents even well-correlated signals from separating the top candidate.
Nine method categories, spanning agreement signals, adaptive approaches, and supervised classifiers, all fail to close the gap across three datasets and two model families (Table~\ref{tab:method_summary}; Appendix~\ref{app:method_coverage}).
Recent work \cite{yao2026consistency} shows task-level correlation ($\rho$ up to 0.47) but does not diagnose when or why it fails at the selection level, nor identify entity-level bypass mechanisms.

The diagnosis points to a structural remedy: since sample-level selection is blocked by $\alpha{\to}0$, we shift granularity from sample to entity.
LP-weighted entity construction ($+0.32$\textendash$1.40$\,pp; Holm $p_{\text{adj}}{=}0.006$ on Few-NERD), cross-model ensemble ($+0.42$\,pp), and regime-specific LP selection ($+1.39$\,pp) bypass the bottleneck; a degeneracy threshold $\theta_{\text{crit}}{=}0.70$ predicts when gains vanish.
These findings rest on controlled experiments across four NER benchmarks (SciERC \cite{luan2018scierc}, Few-NERD \cite{ding2021fewnerd}, CoNLL-2003 \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll}, WNUT-17 \cite{derczynski2017wnut}), two model families (Qwen3-8B, LLaMA-3.1-8B), 4B/14B ablations, $N {\in} \{2, \ldots, 64\}$, with extensions to Qwen2.5-72B and GPT-5.5 zero-shot (\S\ref{sec:scaling}), RE\footnote{RE F1 is confounded by entity span errors: the majority of zero-F1 RE instances reflect upstream NER mismatches rather than relation classification failure (Appendix~\ref{app:re_extension}).} (\S\ref{sec:discussion}), and SQL parsing (87.2\% degeneracy).
